Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-09-11 | AMZN | Hold | -1.2% | -1.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is a Hold at benchmark weight: maintain the existing position (100% of a standard allocation), do not add at $256.78, and do not short a name whose close still sits above a rising 50-day ($255.25) above a rising 200-day ($239.80). Keep both conditional adds but shrink each from +25% to +15-20% of a standard allocation with a hard cap of ~115-120% of benchmark: the pullback add in the $252-254 band (stop $247.45, target $266.66, ~2.2:1) is no longer a blind $253.50 limit — it requires price to hold above $251.26 and show stabilization or a reclaim of $255.25 first — while the breakout add requires a daily close above $258.96-$259.50 on >=32M shares AND the MACD line crossing back above signal, trimming the added tranche if $258 fails for two sessions. Risk ladder is unchanged: close below $251.26 trims 25-30%, below $249.48 cut to half of benchmark, below $239.80-$239.82 exit the long and move to Underweight. Size off core EPS of ~$8.18-8.64 (~30x), not the reported $5.75 quarter; horizon 3-6 months, re-scored on the Q3 print and on the stated technical triggers.

**Investment Thesis**: The debate does not split on direction — the Research Manager, the trader and all three risk seats land on maintenance — so the real dispute is only how much conditional buying to pre-authorize, and on the current record the answer is: less than the trader's plan, more than the conservative's freeze-out.

The operating case is uncontested and I credit it fully: Q2 revenue +19.6% to $200.6B (accelerating from +16.6%), operating income +43.2%, operating margin 13.7% (+230bp), H1 operating income $51.3B (+36.6%), H1 CFO $71.4B (+44.2%), TTM CFO $161.4B (+33%), inventory flat at $38.2B on ~20% revenue growth, SBC down to 3.0% of revenue. Stripping the $50.5B non-cash equity markup, core EPS was still ~$2.16 in Q2 (+29%) and ~$4.09 in H1 (+25%). That rules out Sell and rules out a short — and it also indicts the prior run of Underweight calls, whose five-day alphas were -1.1%, -1.1%, -0.8% and -1.2%: directionally fine but essentially beta, with the 09-03 review conceding its +0.3% alpha cut against the Underweight. The repeated lesson in this name is that heavy de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200 structure (late July-August) forfeited 12-22% of five-day alpha, and that a five-day window cannot score a thesis written for the Q3 print. Hence: hold at weight, pre-commit now to scoring this at the Q3 print over a >=1-month window, and let conditional adds — not a chase — express the upside.

The bear wins the three points that price the equity for the next one to two quarters, and the aggressive desk never repaired them. (1) Earnings quality: $50.5B of $80.9B Q2 pretax income (62%) and $62.8B of $120.7B H1 (52%) came from upward adjustments on equity securities without readily determinable fair value, with that book going $16.2B to $122.3B in six months — a 20% markdown is ~$24B pretax, ~$1.70-1.75 EPS. It also touches cash: H1 cash taxes of $4.0B against $27.8B of book tax expense, so roughly $30.5B of the charge was deferred largely off those unrealized gains, meaning one accounting item lifts both EPS and CFO. (2) Payoff inversion: TTM FCF -$11.6B versus +$13.5B, capex $173.0B (+61%) at 2.3x depreciation, total debt $132.2B (+93% in six months), Q2 interest expense $1,314M (+155%), coverage 37.2x to 20.9x, net interest income -$19M, and $650B of contractual obligations with $78.1B due inside twelve months. Capex-driven negative FCF is a choice, not distress — ~$44B positive net cash ex-leases and 20.9x coverage are not leverage stress — but the financing signature (net new debt ~$56.7B) does not flex downward if AI demand growth slows. (3) Timing: MACD negative and below signal for 19 sessions, six consecutive lower lows from $270.73 to $249.58, price under the VWMA ($257.95) and Bollinger mid-band ($258.96), and the 09-11 +1.94% bounce on only 26.72M shares versus a ~31.9M average while distribution days printed 31.70M and 33.06M.

Where each desk overreached sets the sizing. The aggressive analyst wins the momentum-at-the-margin argument (first MACD-line uptick since 08-11, VWMA decline decelerating from -1.55 to -0.21, heavy volume concentrated on down days — a plausible exhaustion read) but fails on arithmetic: he defends a ~$259.10 entry by invoking the $284-287 post-gap peak when the plan's own first target is $266.66 with $261.12 and $267.56 in between, making the confirmed-breakout trade ~0.96:1, not 2.8:1. You size to the nearest evidence, not the most hopeful outcome — so 125% of benchmark is not underwritten. The conservative analyst is right that a low-volume bounce is "lack of demand until proven otherwise" and right that a $253.50 limit can catch a falling knife with $239.80-$239.82 as the next structural floor — but his fix is self-defeating: demanding a close above $255.25 before adding at $253.50 deletes the entry he is trying to protect, and capping at 110-115% while pre-committing to add only on confirmation is effectively a no-add plan for a business growing operating income 43.2%. The neutral desk resolves this cleanly and gets my vote on mechanics: keep the ~2.2:1 pullback setup (entry $252-254, stop $247.45 under the $249.58 low and the 61.8% retrace at $249.48, target $266.66) but gate it on holding above $251.26 with stabilization or a reclaim of $255.25; keep the breakout add only behind the full three-condition package; shrink each add to +15-20% and cap total exposure at ~115-120%.

Missing evidence is itself part of the decision: no AWS segment revenue or margin, no advertising or retail-margin news, no forward capex or guidance detail, no analyst-rating data, a news sample of 20 of 188 eligible records (~10.6%), and no options-implied positioning, short interest or institutional flow. Normalizing to core EPS of ~$8.18-8.64 puts AMZN near 30x with negative FCF — defensible against 25-29% core growth, but only if the marks do not reverse and capex converts. Upgrade to Overweight only on a volume-confirmed close above $258.96-$259.50 with MACD back above signal plus at least two of: (a) AWS segment growth/margin evidence, (b) forward capex guidance below the $173B TTM run-rate against the $650B obligation book, (c) no markdown in the $122.3B book, (d) cash taxes normalizing toward book tax. Downgrade to Underweight on any markdown/impairment in that book, on cash-tax normalization exposing the CFO flattering, or on: close below $251.26 (trim 25-30%), below $249.48 (half of benchmark), below $239.80-$239.82 (exit the long) — the last is where the rising-200-day structure underpinning the bull case breaks, so it is a thesis failure, not merely a trade failure. No portfolio, holdings or cash context was provided, so all sizing is a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and should flex with the caller's aggregate AI-capex exposure elsewhere.

**Price Target**: 266.66

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the Q3 print (late October) and on the $258.96-259.50 breakout / $251.26-249.48 breakdown triggers, whichever comes first

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -1.1% (raw -1.2%) is a slight negative but essentially beta, and the window is far too short to score a thesis explicitly written for the Q3 print over 3-6 months — Hold-at-weight behaved as designed, delivering no edge in either direction. What it does support is the bear's timing point and the refusal to chase: declining to add at $256.78 ahead of an unconfirmed $258.96-$259.50 breakout avoided a worse entry, and the gated ladder (no trigger on either the pullback add above $251.26 or the breakout) kept the position out of a fading tape without forcing an unnecessary trim above $249.48. The lesson for the next similar setup is that a benchmark-weight Hold in a name with a negative MACD and six consecutive lower lows will mechanically produce roughly -1% alpha when the tape drifts down, so if the desk genuinely expects the distribution phase to resolve lower first, the honest expression is a modest underweight or a smaller core — not a Hold padded with conditional adds that the price action never reaches.

[2026-09-10 | AMZN | Underweight | -0.3% | -0.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Underweight: trim the existing position by roughly one-third to ~60% of a standard allocation (toward ~50% if the caller is concentrated or cannot absorb a gap), executing the majority ratably near the current 251.89 area rather than parking it behind a bounce that the distribution read says is unlikely. Do not short, do not lever, and do not add on the unconfirmed 251.89 touch; the hard strategic stop is a weekly close below 239.60 (200-day 239.62 plus the 239.82 gap floor), and re-entry requires a volume-backed reclaim of 259.38, not a touch of 239.6. Pre-commit now to re-scoring the whole thesis at the late-October Q3 print over a ≥1-month window, so a few sessions of noise is never read as confirmation of the cash-conversion case.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction was not contested by any seat — Research Manager, trader and all three risk analysts land on reduce — so the real decision is how deep and on what execution rules. The bear wins the horizon that governs sizing, and it wins on verifiable data rather than narrative.

What the bear proved, and the bull conceded. (1) The tape: AMZN closed below the 50-day (254.95) on both 09-09 and 09-10, the first break since 07-30; three lower highs at 280.14 → 266.40 → 267.56 and a lower low at 249.58; price 2.43% below VWMA 258.16; MACD histogram re-widening −1.120 → −1.328 → −1.429; RSI 43.62 with no bullish divergence. The Aug 28 +3.97% session on 49.5M shares — heaviest since Aug 3 — was fully retraced in three sessions, and 25.48M shares of drift does not outweigh a 46.1M-share distribution print. (2) The bull's own technical source weights the outcome 45% down / 35% chop / 20% up; his "3:1 payoff" attached no probabilities, so the bear's expected-value arithmetic stands, and the bull's preferred entry (a 3% higher close above 259.40) cannot be paired with a best-case 287.20 exit. (3) The $650B of contractual obligations is a purchase-commitment ladder — capacity, content, energy, logistics — not a revenue backlog; the bull's risk dismissal rested on that misread, and $78.1B due inside twelve months limits how "discretionary" the capex flex really is. (4) The depreciation bill is ahead, not behind: ~$54.2B/quarter capex against a $20.0B D&A run-rate is 2.7x, implying steady-state D&A trends toward ~$50B/quarter, so ~230bp of margin expansion is being extrapolated off a lagging charge. (5) "Net cash" excludes $96.3B of operating leases; including them the balance sheet is nearer ~$67B net debt than +$29.7B net cash, with long-term debt up 93% in six months and interest expense +155%. (6) Valuation was never answered: ~26–29x annualized adjusted earnings, TTM FCF −$11.6B, no dividend, no buyback — the longest-duration, most capex-intensive, negative-FCF mega-cap in the group, and the exact profile that de-rates first with oil above $101 and 10-year yields at multi-year highs. The bull calling the Sept 9 decline "macro noise" concedes the point rather than rebutting it.

Why the direction is Underweight and not Sell. The bull won two things outright and the bear conceded both: the primary structure is intact (200-day at 239.62 rising every session since late June, 50/200 spread +6.4%, unbroken higher lows 196.00 → 199.14 → 226.16) and the operating engine is accelerating (Q2 revenue +19.6%, operating income $27.46B +43.2%, margin 13.7% +230bp, H1 operating income +36.6%, marketing down to 5.8% of revenue, SBC down in absolute dollars — margins expanding 230bp while D&A ran at 10.0% of revenue, +31% y/y). There is no solvency or permanent-capital-loss case, the weekly-close invalidation below 239.6 has not triggered, and the record in this name is unambiguous that heavy de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200 structure (07-22 to 07-30) cost 12–22% of five-day alpha while measured trims (08-12, 08-21) were neutral to modestly positive. Shorting a franchise growing operating income 40% into a rising 200-day with bandwidth compressed to 6.25% is the wrong risk, so a real core stays. Why not Hold: the debate did not end balanced. The bear won the near- and intermediate-term questions on verifiable data, while the bull's counterarguments were structural or forward projections, and full weight at 251.89 is roughly 1% to the first downside trigger (249.58) against 3% to genuine repair (259.38), with an air pocket underneath.

Where I side with each seat on execution. The aggressive seat is right that the aggressive action and the prudent action are the same trade here, and right that a ratable near-market tranche is mandatory — the documented failure mode in this book (8/25 GOOGL, 8/20 AMZN) is gating a first tranche behind a 1% rally into resistance and converting a correct call into relative drag. He is too casual about event risk, however. The conservative seat lands the two amendments that actually change the plan and I adopt both: the 239.60 stop is defined only on a quiet day (AMZN has printed a −9% gap on Feb 6 and +12.5% on Jul 31, and late-October earnings will swing on mark-to-model adjustments to a $122.3B private book), and the second tranche cannot depend on a bounce the bearish thesis says will not arrive. The neutral seat supplies the correct rule set: keep the ~60% core conditional on the caller's single-name risk budget rather than as an automatic number, put a 5–10 session fallback on the middle tranche (execute at market or on a failed bounce below the 10-day EMA 256.55 if 254.95–259.38 never trades), require a confirmed close below 249.58 — preferably on >35M shares — for the final tranche rather than reading the light-volume 09-10 undercut as a breakdown, and require confirmation, not a touch, for re-entry. I reject the aggressive seat's "highest-confluence support" re-entry at 239.6–241.0: the report is explicit those are observed clusters, not validated bounce points, and buying a touch of a moving average with negative FCF and a rising discount rate is how a de-risk gets re-levered.

Sizing. Trim to ~60% of a standard allocation, i.e. cut the existing position by about one-third: roughly one-third of the trim near 251.89, one-third into 254.95–259.38 with the time/price fallback, and the rest only on a confirmed break of 249.58. A caller who is concentrated, levered elsewhere in AI capex, or unwilling to carry an October gap should go to ~50%. Total single-name risk on AMZN at or below ~1.0–1.5% of portfolio value, derived off the 239.60 weekly-close stop, and explicitly sized to a stress gap toward 226–235 rather than to the stop itself, because the stop is not gap-proof. No short, no leverage, no undefined-risk options.

What would change the call. Upgrade toward standard weight requires all of: a close above 259.40 on >40M shares with VWMA 258.16 and the 20-day 259.38 reclaimed and a higher low in the MACD histogram; then Overweight on a subsequent hold of 267.45 (38.2% Fib) as support. Fundamentally, a Q3 print showing capex plateauing at or below the $54.2B Q2 figure with AWS re-accelerating and operating income still +35–40% would force a re-underwrite, because the bull's operating case will then have survived the depreciation test. Cut to a token position and stand aside on a weekly close below 239.6 (that invalidates the higher-low sequence and the July gap), and exit the residual if Q3 pairs a capex guide-up with decelerating AWS growth — that is the combination that compresses the multiple.

Data I am not underwriting, flagged rather than papered over: the news feed is 20 of 177 records, all dated Sept 9, with nothing from Sept 3–8, so neither the bull's "no positive catalyst" nor the bear's policy-headwind narrative is properly sampled; the Ohio data-center incentive review is unquantified and contingent; the NTSB / Prime Air item has no established financial materiality; insider-transaction data is unavailable, so neither side can claim or deny an insider bid; no AWS segment revenue, margin or backlog appears in the dataset, leaving the demand side of the capex program as inference; the identity and valuation inputs for the $122.3B non-marketable equity book are undisclosed, and a markdown there would arrive as a gap and is a Sell trigger; and with no portfolio, holdings or cash context, all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and should flex with the caller's aggregate AI-capex exposure elsewhere — trimming AMZN while holding NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL and neoclouds at full weight would be optics, not risk management.

**Price Target**: 246.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print over a ≥1-month window

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -0.9% (raw -0.3%) modestly supports the Underweight call on a relative basis, but the window is far too short to judge a 3–6 month thesis or the 246 target. It supports the near-term distribution/tape read and the ratable-trim execution rule, while leaving the capex/D&A, FCF, and valuation case untested. Next time, pre-commit to scoring the thesis only over the stated horizon or at the Q3 print, and use 5-day alpha solely to audit execution rather than as confirmation.
